stem: An added ROS2 timing test reports a mean end-to-end latency of 2 ms for a task with a 10 ms deadline, but supplies no worst-case bound or scheduler/workload analysis. Which conclusion follows from the source’s real-time support claim?

Selecting reliable message delivery establishes the 10 ms deadline even without a timing bound.
ROS2 supports real-time-oriented design, but the mean alone does not establish a 10 ms deadline guarantee for the complete system.

assumptions: The timing values are added illustration, not measured source performance. No worst-case latency, jitter bound or workload/configuration proof is supplied.

stem: Compare two added navigation logs. Run A: one simulator, correct loaded map, initialized AMCL with aligned scans, current transforms on simulation time 40 s, and an accepted goal; a newly sensed barrier blocks the route. The allowed one recovery and one replan have completed, and the planner returns NO_VALID_PATH. Run B: after a simulator reset, /clock is 6 s but the only cached transform is stamped 73 s from the previous run; the map is loaded and the stack reports active, but the controller is waiting for a time-consistent transform. Which diagnosis/action pair is supported?

options.text: A: reset the initial AMCL pose despite aligned scans and retry without a limit. B: clear obstacle costmaps but keep the pre-reset transform for control.
A: report this goal’s route failure after the exhausted retry. B: restore consistent simulation-time/state data and localization transforms before attempting motion.
A: keep issuing controller commands along the old path because the goal was accepted. B: restart only the planner and reuse the 73 s transform because the map is unchanged.

assumptions: Both logs and the one-recovery/one-replan budget are added, not the exact Nav2 default tree or source experiment.
Time-consistent transforms are required before executing a command. Run B has no current valid transform; the old transform must not be treated as current merely because the static map is unchanged.
Run A has no remaining feasible route after its permitted retry. Stack active, goal accepted and goal reached are distinct states. No physical or simulated robot is operated.

stem: In an added Gazebo robot design, the declared topic /sim_scan carries simulated range observations out to ROS navigation, while /drive_command carries ROS velocity requests into the simulated drive. Which plugin arrangement preserves the source’s sensor-output and motor-input distinction?

options.text: The range plugin publishes its measured distances on /drive_command as if they were commanded velocity, while the drive plugin subscribes to /sim_scan for actuation.
A GUI-only plugin changes the visible robot colour when /drive_command arrives, while no plugin feeds sensor observations to navigation.
A sensor-side plugin publishes /sim_scan to ROS consumers, while a drive/model plugin receives /drive_command and applies it to the simulated robot.
A sensor-side plugin subscribes to /sim_scan as its only data source, while the drive plugin publishes /drive_command without receiving a controller request.

assumptions: /sim_scan and /drive_command are explicitly added illustrative topic names, not names printed in the slides or an executed package.
Message contents/types, timestamps, frames and controller-to-plugin conversion must be compatible as declared; no inference of a specific existing plugin API.
